A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the problem of minimizing the number of measurements is very hard in the sense that the competitive ratio and approximation ratio are both at least logarithmic, and that the best strategy for the offline network verification model seems to be a simple greedy algorithm.
, in both of our models, the greedy strategies perform well, but the competitive ratio of the online problem is not constant, while the approximation ratio of the offline problem is constant.
, for the network discovery problem, the greedy strategy that minimizes the number of measurements is not necessarily the best strategy in terms of the competitive ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the greedy strategies are very close to the theoretically proven bounds and perform well in practice.
